hints.content: Any two segments tangent to a circle from a common endpoint are congruent.
Segments $\overline{AC}$ and $\overline{AB}$ are both tangent to circle $O$  because $\angle A$ is circumscribed about circle $O$.

question.content:
Angle $A$ is circumscribed about circle $O$.

**What is the length of $\overline{AC}$?**  
[[☃ numeric-input 1]] units



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A circle centered around point O. Point A is outside of the circle. Segment O B and segment O C are both radii of the circle. There are line segments that connect point A to points B and C, creating segment A B and segment A C. There is a point D on the circle that lies opposite to point A. There are chords connecting points B and C to point D, creating segment B D and segment C D. Angle B D C measures sixty-five degrees. Segment C D is five units. Segment O B is three units. Segment A B is six units.

answers.message: This is the length of AO.  Any two segments tangent to a circle from a common endpoint are congruent.
